22/// PdfCraft patch: largest image drawn, in pixels (2^28 ≈ 268 MP, well above real page images).
23const MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS: u64 = 1 << 28;
24
25/// PdfCraft patch: source axes allowed into CatmullRom planning. Unlike the final pixmap,
26/// sources need not fit u16: a 65536-pixel strip can safely shrink to a 16-pixel image.
27/// This resource cap follows the existing CCITT column limit; the filter-work estimate below
28/// additionally bounds tables/scratch before entering the opaque PicScale planner.
29const MAX_RESAMPLING_SOURCE_SIDE: u32 = 1 << 20;
30const MAX_RESAMPLING_PLAN_BYTES: usize = 128 << 20;
31
32/// PdfCraft patch: source, intermediate and RGBA byte lengths, independent of backend sides.
33fn source_byte_len(width: u32, height: u32, channels: usize, max_pixels: u64) -> Option<usize> {
34    if width == 0 || height == 0 || !matches!(channels, 1 | 3 | 4) {
35        return None;
36    }
37    let pixels = u64::from(width).checked_mul(u64::from(height))?;
38    if pixels > max_pixels {
39        return None;
40    }
41    let pixels = usize::try_from(pixels).ok()?;
42    let rgba_len = pixels.checked_mul(4)?;
43    if rgba_len > isize::MAX as usize {
44        return None;
45    }
46    pixels.checked_mul(channels)
47}
48
49/// PdfCraft patch: only final pixmaps/padded glyphs need to fit the backend's u16 sides.
50fn image_byte_len(width: u32, height: u32, channels: usize, max_pixels: u64) -> Option<usize> {
51    if width > u32::from(u16::MAX) || height > u32::from(u16::MAX) {
52        return None;
53    }
54    source_byte_len(width, height, channels, max_pixels)
55}

57/// PdfCraft patch: conservative CatmullRom planning work for one axis in PicScale 0.7.12.
58/// Its four-tap kernel grows on downscaling. Include float/32-aligned i16 weights, temporary
59/// float/f64/usize tap arrays and two copies of the bounds. This is a size estimate, not a
60/// fallible reserve inside PicScale or a bound on total renderer memory.
61fn filter_plan_bytes(source: u32, target: u32) -> Option<usize> {
62    if source == target {
63        return Some(0);
64    }
65    let (source, target) = (usize::try_from(source).ok()?, usize::try_from(target).ok()?);
66    if target == 0 {
67        return None;
68    }
69    let taps = source.checked_mul(4)?.div_ceil(target).max(4);
70    let aligned_taps = taps.div_ceil(32).checked_mul(32)?;
71    let float_weights = taps.checked_mul(target)?.checked_mul(size_of::<f32>())?;
72    let fixed_weights = aligned_taps.checked_mul(target)?.checked_mul(size_of::<i16>())?;
73    let tap_scratch = taps.checked_mul(size_of::<f32>() + size_of::<f64>() + size_of::<usize>())?;
74    let bounds = target.checked_mul(4)?.checked_mul(size_of::<usize>())?;
75    float_weights.checked_add(fixed_weights)?.checked_add(tap_scratch)?.checked_add(bounds)
76}

78/// PdfCraft patch: alpha-aware RGBA plans also need source-sized premultiplication scratch.
79/// Bound the combined scratch before planning, including a conservative crossed intermediate
80/// (or four rows for a short target) when both convolution axes change.
81fn resampling_scratch_byte_len(source: (u32, u32), target: (u32, u32), channels: usize, max_pixels: u64) -> Option<usize> {
82    if source == target {
83        return Some(0);
84    }
85    let alpha = if channels == 4 { source_byte_len(source.0, source.1, channels, max_pixels)? } else { 0 };
86    let filter = if source.0 != target.0 && source.1 != target.1 { source_byte_len(source.0, target.1.max(4), channels, max_pixels)? } else { 0 };
87    let len = alpha.checked_add(filter)?;
88    let limit = max_pixels.saturating_mul(4).min(isize::MAX as u64);
89    if u64::try_from(len).ok()? > limit {
90        return None;
91    }
92    Some(len)
93}

95/// PdfCraft patch: validate output, crossed intermediate and filter-work bounds before planning.
96/// Source width × target height also bounds PicScale's smaller single-threaded four-row scratch.
97/// Nearest-neighbour (`!interpolate`) has none of those: it copies source pixels into the target,
98/// so only the source and target buffers are bounded.
99fn resampling_byte_len(
100    source: (u32, u32),
101    target: (u32, u32),
102    channels: usize,
103    data_len: usize,
104    max_pixels: u64,
105    interpolate: bool,
106) -> Option<usize> {
107    if source_byte_len(source.0, source.1, channels, max_pixels)? != data_len {
108        return None;
109    }
110    let target_len = image_byte_len(target.0, target.1, channels, max_pixels)?;
111    if !interpolate {
112        return Some(target_len);
113    }
114    resampling_scratch_byte_len(source, target, channels, max_pixels)?;
115    source_byte_len(source.0, target.1, channels, max_pixels)?;
116    if source.0 > MAX_RESAMPLING_SOURCE_SIDE || source.1 > MAX_RESAMPLING_SOURCE_SIDE {
117        return None;
118    }
119    let plan_bytes = filter_plan_bytes(source.0, target.0)?.checked_add(filter_plan_bytes(source.1, target.1)?)?;
120    if plan_bytes > MAX_RESAMPLING_PLAN_BYTES {
121        return None;
122    }
123    Some(target_len)
124}

126/// PdfCraft patch: image dimensions selected before allocating resampling buffers.
127/// Exported for PdfCraft's small, metadata-only regression tests. `None` rejects invalid
128/// sources/scales or an over-budget target/intermediate; the caller may retain a valid source.
129/// `interpolate` selects the Catmull-Rom limits; nearest-neighbour (`false`) skips them.
130#[doc(hidden)]
131pub fn image_resampling_size(
132    width: u32,
133    height: u32,
134    channels: usize,
135    data_len: usize,
136    x_scale: f32,
137    y_scale: f32,
138    max_pixels: u64,
139    interpolate: bool,
140) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
141    if !x_scale.is_finite() || !y_scale.is_finite() || x_scale <= 0.0 || y_scale <= 0.0 {
142        return None;
143    }
144    let target = if x_scale < 1.0 || y_scale < 1.0 {
145        let side = |size: u32, scale: f32| (size as f32 * scale).ceil().max(1.0).min((u16::MAX / 2) as f32) as u32;
146        (side(width, x_scale), side(height, y_scale))
147    } else {
148        (width, height)
149    };
150    resampling_byte_len((width, height), target, channels, data_len, max_pixels, interpolate)?;
151    Some(target)
152}

154/// PdfCraft patch: allocation failures in image conversion/resampling keep the renderer alive.
155fn image_buffer(len: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
156    let mut out = Vec::new();
157    out.try_reserve_exact(len).ok()?;
158    Some(out)
159}

161/// PdfCraft patch: `mask` sampled onto the grid of a `width` × `height` image (no side smaller
162/// than the mask's). Each image sample takes the mask sample under its centre or, for a mask that
163/// asks for `/Interpolate`, the bilinear blend of the four around it, so the mask's edges stay as
164/// smooth as when it was enlarged on its own. `None` for an empty side, an image side smaller than
165/// the mask's, or a buffer over the limits.
166fn mask_on_image_grid(mask: &LumaData, width: u32, height: u32) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
167    if width == 0 || height == 0 || mask.width == 0 || mask.height == 0 {
168        return None;
169    }
170    let mut out = image_buffer(source_byte_len(width, height, 1, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS)?)?;
171    let columns = grid_axis(mask.width, width, mask.interpolate)?;
172    let rows = grid_axis(mask.height, height, mask.interpolate)?;
173    let mask_width = mask.width as usize;
174    let row = |y: usize| {
175        let start = y.checked_mul(mask_width)?;
176        mask.data.get(start..start.checked_add(mask_width)?)
177    };
178    let one = u64::from(GRID_ONE);
179    for &(y0, y1, fy) in &rows {
180        let (top, bottom, fy) = (row(y0)?, row(y1)?, u64::from(fy));
181        for &(x0, x1, fx) in &columns {
182            let fx = u64::from(fx);
183            let blend = |r: &[u8]| Some(u64::from(*r.get(x0)?) * (one - fx) + u64::from(*r.get(x1)?) * fx);
184            // At most 255 × GRID_ONE², so the sum fits in a u64 and the result in a u8.
185            let v = (blend(top)? * (one - fy) + blend(bottom)? * fy + one * one / 2) / (one * one);
186            out.push(v.min(255) as u8);
187        }
188    }
189    Some(out)
190}
191
192/// PdfCraft patch: fixed-point unit of [`grid_axis`]'s blend weights.
193const GRID_ONE: u32 = 1 << 16;
194
195/// PdfCraft patch: for each of `dst` samples (`dst >= src`) taken from `src` along one axis, the
196/// two source samples it lies between and the weight of the second, in [`GRID_ONE`] units.
197/// Centres line up: target `t` lies at `(t + ½)·src/dst − ½` source samples, held to the ends.
198/// Without `smooth` both are the nearest sample, so the weight does not matter.
199fn grid_axis(src: u32, dst: u32, smooth: bool) -> Option<Vec<(usize, usize, u32)>> {
200    if src == 0 || dst < src {
201        return None;
202    }
203    let mut out = Vec::new();
204    out.try_reserve_exact(dst as usize).ok()?;
205    let last = u64::from(src - 1) << 16;
206    for t in 0..dst {
207        if !smooth {
208            let s = nearest_source_index(src, dst, t);
209            out.push((s, s, 0));
210            continue;
211        }
212        // In u128, as `(2t + 1)·src·2^16` can pass 2^64 for a long side; the quotient is at
213        // most `src·2^16`, so it fits back in a u64.
214        let centre = ((2 * u128::from(t) + 1) * u128::from(src) << 16) / (2 * u128::from(dst));
215        let at = u64::try_from(centre).ok()?.saturating_sub(u64::from(GRID_ONE / 2)).min(last);
216        let s = (at >> 16) as usize;
217        out.push((s, (s + 1).min(src as usize - 1), (at & 0xFFFF) as u32));
218    }
219    Some(out)
220}

222/// PdfCraft patch (#624): the source index that PicScale's nearest-neighbour plan copies for
223/// destination `index` of `dst` samples taken from `src`. It is the same fixed-point centre
224/// sampling as `ResampleNearestPlan`, so these are the samples a nearest resize would copy.
225fn nearest_source_index(src: u32, dst: u32, index: u32) -> usize {
226    let step = (u64::from(src) << 32) / u64::from(dst);
227    ((u64::from(index) * step + (step >> 1)) >> 32) as usize
228}
229
230/// PdfCraft patch (#624): nearest-resizes a colour image and its same-sized soft mask straight
231/// into premultiplied RGBA of `target` size. Colour and mask come from the same source pixel, so
232/// this equals a nearest resize of the expanded RGBA followed by premultiplying each pixel.
233fn nearest_premultiplied_rgba(color: &ImageData, alpha: &[u8], source: (u32, u32), target: (u32, u32)) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
234    let (samples, channels) = match color {
235        ImageData::Luma(luma) => (luma.data.as_slice(), 1),
236        ImageData::Rgb(rgb) => (rgb.data.as_slice(), 3),
237    };
238    let mut out = image_buffer(image_byte_len(target.0, target.1, 4, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS)?)?;
239    for ty in 0..target.1 {
240        let sy = nearest_source_index(source.1, target.1, ty);
241        for tx in 0..target.0 {
242            let si = sy * source.0 as usize + nearest_source_index(source.0, target.0, tx);
243            let [r, g, b] = match samples.get(si * channels..si * channels + channels)? {
244                [v] => [*v; 3],
245                [r, g, b] => [*r, *g, *b],
246                _ => return None,
247            };
248            let a = *alpha.get(si)?;
249            out.extend_from_slice(&AlphaColor::from_rgba8(r, g, b, a).premultiply().to_rgba8().to_u8_array());
250        }
251    }
252    Some(out)
253}

255/// PdfCraft patch: the shorter side, in samples, from which an image that did not ask for
256/// `/Interpolate` is still smoothed when enlarged. A page scanned at 72 dpi is 612 samples wide;
257/// icons, QR codes and pixel art are usually far smaller and keep their hard pixels.
258const SMOOTHED_IMAGE_SIDE: u32 = 512;
259
260/// PdfCraft patch: the scale above which such an image counts as enlarged. A scan drawn at its own
261/// resolution can come out a few ulps above 1 (the scale is an `f32`: a 192 dpi scan on a 2×
262/// display at 100%), and sampled bilinearly at a half-pixel offset it blurred by half a pixel.
263/// Below 1% nearest-neighbour repeats at most one sample in a hundred.
264const SMOOTHED_IMAGE_SCALE: f32 = 1.01;
265
266/// PdfCraft patch: fixed-point unit of [`area_shrink`]'s weights.
267const AREA_ONE: u64 = 1 << 16;
268
269/// PdfCraft patch: the source samples target sample `t` covers when `src` samples shrink to `dst`
270/// (`dst <= src`), with their weights in [`AREA_ONE`] units. Target `t` spans `[t·src, (t+1)·src)`
271/// and source `s` spans `[s·dst, (s+1)·dst)`, both in units of 1/(src·dst) of the axis, so every
272/// overlap is exact. The weights are differences of one rounded running sum, so they add up to
273/// exactly [`AREA_ONE`] and a flat area keeps its exact value.
274fn area_taps(src: u32, dst: u32, t: u32) -> impl Iterator<Item = (usize, u64)> {
275    let (src, dst, t) = (u64::from(src), u64::from(dst), u64::from(t));
276    // `t < dst <= src <= 2^28` (MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS), so every product below fits in a u64.
277    let (lo, hi) = (t * src, (t + 1) * src);
278    let fixed = move |x: u64| (x * AREA_ONE + src / 2) / src;
279    (lo / dst..hi.div_ceil(dst)).map(move |s| {
280        let from = (s * dst).max(lo) - lo;
281        let to = ((s + 1) * dst).min(hi) - lo;
282        (s as usize, fixed(to) - fixed(from))
283    })
284}

286/// PdfCraft patch: [`area_taps`] of every target sample of one axis, worked out once: for each
287/// target, the first source sample it covers and the weights of the samples from there on (the
288/// samples a target covers are consecutive). There are at most `src + dst` taps in all.
289struct AreaAxis {
290    first: Vec<usize>,
291    /// Where each target's weights start in `weights`, and where the last one's end.
292    offsets: Vec<usize>,
293    weights: Vec<u32>,
294}
295
296impl AreaAxis {
297    fn new(src: u32, dst: u32) -> Option<Self> {
298        let n = dst as usize;
299        let (mut first, mut offsets, mut weights) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new());
300        first.try_reserve_exact(n).ok()?;
301        offsets.try_reserve_exact(n.checked_add(1)?).ok()?;
302        weights.try_reserve_exact((src as usize).checked_add(n.checked_mul(2)?)?).ok()?;
303        offsets.push(0);
304        for t in 0..dst {
305            let mut start = None;
306            for (s, w) in area_taps(src, dst, t) {
307                start.get_or_insert(s);
308                // A weight is at most AREA_ONE, so it fits in a u32.
309                weights.push(w as u32);
310            }
311            first.push(start?);
312            offsets.push(weights.len());
313        }
314        Some(Self { first, offsets, weights })
315    }
316
317    /// Target `t`'s first source sample and its weights.
318    fn get(&self, t: usize) -> Option<(usize, &[u32])> {
319        let (lo, hi) = (*self.offsets.get(t)?, *self.offsets.get(t.checked_add(1)?)?);
320        Some((*self.first.get(t)?, self.weights.get(lo..hi)?))
321    }
322}

324/// PdfCraft patch: shrinks `N`-channel samples from `source` to `target` (no side larger than its
325/// source side) by area averaging: each target sample is the mean of the source it covers,
326/// weighted by how much of it it covers. Nothing is invented between samples, which is what
327/// `/Interpolate` governs (ISO 32000-2 §8.9.5.3, for images drawn above their resolution), and
328/// nothing is dropped: nearest-neighbour keeps one sample in N per axis, so a scan shown at screen
329/// size lost the strokes of its text. Premultiplied input stays premultiplied. `None` if nothing
330/// shrinks, the sizes don't fit or a buffer cannot be allocated.
331fn area_shrink<const N: usize>(data: &[u8], source: (u32, u32), target: (u32, u32)) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
332    if data.len() != source_byte_len(source.0, source.1, N, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS)? {
333        return None;
334    }
335    let row_len = (source.0 as usize).checked_mul(N)?;
336    area_shrink_rows::<N>(source, target, |s, row| {
337        let start = s.checked_mul(row_len)?;
338        row.copy_from_slice(data.get(start..start.checked_add(row_len)?)?);
339        Some(())
340    })
341}
342
343/// PdfCraft patch: [`area_shrink`] of a colour image under its same-size soft mask (a stencil's
344/// ink under the stencil, or an image under a mask sampled onto its grid), premultiplied a source
345/// row at a time as it is averaged. The result equals premultiplying the expanded RGBA and
346/// shrinking that, without building it: a 10718 × 13701 stencil shown at page size peaked at
347/// 1.16 GB with the full-resolution RGBA, which is 587 MB.
348fn area_shrink_premultiplied(color: &ImageData, alpha: &[u8], source: (u32, u32), target: (u32, u32)) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
349    let (samples, channels) = match color {
350        ImageData::Luma(luma) => (luma.data.as_slice(), 1),
351        ImageData::Rgb(rgb) => (rgb.data.as_slice(), 3),
352    };
353    if samples.len() != source_byte_len(source.0, source.1, channels, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS)?
354        || alpha.len() != source_byte_len(source.0, source.1, 1, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS)?
355    {
356        return None;
357    }
358    let width = source.0 as usize;
359    area_shrink_rows::<4>(source, target, |s, row| {
360        let start = s.checked_mul(width)?;
361        let end = start.checked_add(width)?;
362        let colors = samples.get(start.checked_mul(channels)?..end.checked_mul(channels)?)?;
363        let alphas = alpha.get(start..end)?;
364        for ((out, px), a) in row.chunks_exact_mut(4).zip(colors.chunks_exact(channels)).zip(alphas) {
365            let [r, g, b] = match px {
366                [v] => [*v; 3],
367                [r, g, b] => [*r, *g, *b],
368                _ => return None,
369            };
370            out.copy_from_slice(&AlphaColor::from_rgba8(r, g, b, *a).premultiply().to_rgba8().to_u8_array());
371        }
372        Some(())
373    })
374}

376/// PdfCraft patch: the area shrink behind [`area_shrink`], reading source row `s` through
377/// `read_row(s, row)` into a buffer of one row. Each target row averages the source rows it
378/// covers, and that row is shrunk across at once with taps worked out once per image, so work
379/// memory is one source row of samples, one of `u32` accumulators, one shrunk row and the
380/// horizontal taps (at most `sw + 2 × tw`): never the image. A side over
381/// `MAX_RESAMPLING_SOURCE_SIDE` is refused, so none of it exceeds a few times one source row.
382fn area_shrink_rows<const N: usize>(
383    source: (u32, u32),
384    target: (u32, u32),
385    mut read_row: impl FnMut(usize, &mut [u8]) -> Option<()>,
386) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
387    let ((sw, sh), (tw, th)) = (source, target);
388    // A side over MAX_RESAMPLING_SOURCE_SIDE would make the accumulator row and the tap table
389    // several times larger than the samples (a 2^27 × 2 image of zeros is a tiny file).
390    if tw == 0 || th == 0 || tw > sw || th > sh || (tw, th) == (sw, sh) || sw > MAX_RESAMPLING_SOURCE_SIDE || sh > MAX_RESAMPLING_SOURCE_SIDE {
391        return None;
392    }
393    let row_len = (sw as usize).checked_mul(N)?;
394    let zeroed = |len: usize| {
395        let mut v = image_buffer(len)?;
396        v.resize(len, 0);
397        Some(v)
398    };
399    let (mut source_row, mut shrunk_row) = (zeroed(row_len)?, image_buffer(row_len)?);
400    let mut acc: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
401    acc.try_reserve_exact(row_len).ok()?;
402    acc.resize(row_len, 0);
403    // The taps depend only on the widths, so they are worked out once, not again for each row.
404    let taps = if tw == sw { None } else { Some(AreaAxis::new(sw, tw)?) };
405    let out_len = match taps {
406        None => source_byte_len(tw, th, N, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS)?,
407        Some(_) => image_byte_len(tw, th, N, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS)?,
408    };
409    let mut out = image_buffer(out_len)?;
410    // Weights sum to AREA_ONE (2^16) and samples are at most 255, so every sum fits in a u32.
411    let round = |acc: u32| ((acc + (AREA_ONE as u32) / 2) >> 16).min(255) as u8;
412    // The last source row read: neighbouring target rows share the row on their boundary.
413    let mut loaded = None;
414    for t in 0..th {
415        // Vertical: the whole source rows target row `t` covers, averaged.
416        let row: &[u8] = if th == sh {
417            read_row(t as usize, &mut source_row)?;
418            &source_row
419        } else {
420            acc.fill(0);
421            for (s, w) in area_taps(sh, th, t) {
422                if loaded != Some(s) {
423                    read_row(s, &mut source_row)?;
424                    loaded = Some(s);
425                }
426                // A weight is at most AREA_ONE, so it fits in a u32.
427                let w = w as u32;
428                for (a, v) in acc.iter_mut().zip(&source_row) {
429                    *a += w * u32::from(*v);
430                }
431            }
432            shrunk_row.clear();
433            shrunk_row.extend(acc.iter().map(|a| round(*a)));
434            &shrunk_row
435        };
436        // Horizontal: that row shrunk to `tw` samples.
437        let Some(taps) = &taps else {
438            out.extend_from_slice(row);
439            continue;
440        };
441        for x in 0..tw as usize {
442            let (first, weights) = taps.get(x)?;
443            let samples = row.get(first * N..(first + weights.len()) * N)?;
444            let mut acc = [0_u32; N];
445            for (w, px) in weights.iter().zip(samples.chunks_exact(N)) {
446                for (a, v) in acc.iter_mut().zip(px) {
447                    *a += w * u32::from(*v);
448                }
449            }
450            out.extend(acc.map(round));
451        }
452    }
453    Some(out)
454}
455
456/// PdfCraft patch: [`area_shrink`] for an image's pixel format. If it cannot run, the image keeps
457/// its source resolution, as when [`Renderer::resize_image_data`] fails.
458fn area_resize(data: Vec<u8>, source: (u32, u32), target: (u32, u32), format: ImagePixelFormat) -> (Vec<u8>, u32, u32) {
459    let shrunk = match format {
460        ImagePixelFormat::Luma => area_shrink::<1>(&data, source, target),
461        ImagePixelFormat::Rgb => area_shrink::<3>(&data, source, target),
462        ImagePixelFormat::Rgba => area_shrink::<4>(&data, source, target),
463    };
464    match shrunk {
465        Some(out) => (out, target.0, target.1),
466        None => {
467            log::warn!("Image area shrink failed or exceeded its buffer limit; falling back to source data");
468            (data, source.0, source.1)
469        }
470    }
471}
472
473/// PdfCraft patch: premultiplies straight RGBA samples in place.
474fn premultiply_rgba(rgba: &mut [u8]) {
475    let (chunks, _) = rgba.as_chunks_mut::<4>();
476    for chunk in chunks {
477        let [r, g, b, a] = *chunk;
478        *chunk = AlphaColor::from_rgba8(r, g, b, a).premultiply().to_rgba8().to_u8_array();
479    }
480}
481
482/// PdfCraft patch: most pieces one dashed stroke may be cut into. Stroke expansion keeps every
483/// dash, so a pattern that is tiny next to its path asks for billions: a fuzzed `/D [[11] 0]` on
484/// a line from x = 92234775807 allocated over 5 GB, and `[0.000001] 0 d` on a 20 pt line over
485/// 10 GB. Measured in release builds: a stroke cut into 250,000 pieces renders in about 16 ms and
486/// 75 MB at its peak (a million took 80 ms and 290 MB). Dotted and dashed lines in real documents
487/// stay far below this.
488const MAX_DASHES_PER_STROKE: f64 = 250_000.0;
489
490/// PdfCraft patch: the dash pattern to stroke `path` with. Empty (a solid line) when the pattern
491/// is invalid, or when it could cut the path into more than [`MAX_DASHES_PER_STROKE`] pieces.
492/// ISO 32000-2 §8.4.3.6 requires nonnegative entries that are not all zero; a pattern whose
493/// period isn't positive (`[-1 -1] 0 d`) made kurbo's search for the starting dash loop for ever.
494fn usable_dash_pattern(path: &BezPath, dashes: &[f32]) -> Vec<f64> {
495    if dashes.iter().any(|d| !d.is_finite() || *d < 0.0) {
496        return Vec::new();
497    }
498    let sum: f64 = dashes.iter().map(|d| f64::from(*d)).sum();
499    // kurbo repeats an odd-length pattern once, as SVG does, so a period covers it twice.
500    let (period, per_period) = if dashes.len() % 2 == 1 { (2.0 * sum, dashes.len().saturating_mul(2)) } else { (sum, dashes.len()) };
501    if !period.is_finite() || period <= 0.0 {
502        return Vec::new();
503    }
504    let (length, restarts) = control_polygon_length(path);
505    // kurbo restarts the pattern at every subpath and after every `ClosePath`, so each restart
506    // can begin up to a whole period of pieces however short its segment is.
507    let pieces = (length / period + restarts as f64) * per_period as f64;
508    if !pieces.is_finite() || pieces > MAX_DASHES_PER_STROKE {
509        return Vec::new();
510    }
511    dashes.iter().map(|d| f64::from(*d)).collect()
512}
513
514/// PdfCraft patch: the length of `path`'s control polygon, which a curve never exceeds, and how
515/// many times kurbo restarts a dash pattern along it (each `MoveTo` and `ClosePath`).
516fn control_polygon_length(path: &BezPath) -> (f64, usize) {
517    let (mut length, mut restarts) = (0.0, 0usize);
518    let (mut start, mut last) = (Point::ORIGIN, Point::ORIGIN);
519    for el in path.elements() {
520        match *el {
521            kurbo::PathEl::MoveTo(p) => {
522                (start, last) = (p, p);
523                restarts = restarts.saturating_add(1);
524            }
525            kurbo::PathEl::LineTo(p) => {
526                length += last.distance(p);
527                last = p;
528            }
529            kurbo::PathEl::QuadTo(c, p) => {
530                length += last.distance(c) + c.distance(p);
531                last = p;
532            }
533            kurbo::PathEl::CurveTo(c1, c2, p) => {
534                length += last.distance(c1) + c1.distance(c2) + c2.distance(p);
535                last = p;
536            }
537            kurbo::PathEl::ClosePath => {
538                length += last.distance(start);
539                last = start;
540                restarts = restarts.saturating_add(1);
541            }
542        }
543    }
544    (length, restarts)
545}

547/// PdfCraft patch: how far, in user space, drawing may place geometry outside a path's exact
548/// outline. vello expands strokes to a tolerance of at most 0.25 user units (`TOL / max(|a|, |d|,
549/// 1)` in vello_common's `flatten::stroke`), and kurbo approximates round joins and caps to 1e-3.
550/// Fills are flattened into chords, which stay inside the outline's bounds.
551const DRAW_SLACK: f64 = 0.5;
552
553/// PdfCraft patch: previews skip images below this target area in device pixels: redrawing
554/// them at full detail costs a decode and a resample each for pixels nobody can see.
555const PREVIEW_MIN_IMAGE_AREA: u32 = 16;

558    /// PdfCraft patch: whether [`may_paint_canvas`] may skip paths on this thread. Turned off
559    /// only by PdfCraft's regression test, which renders each tile with and without skipping.
560    static SKIP_OFFSCREEN_PATHS: std::cell::Cell<bool> = const { std::cell::Cell::new(true) };
561}

563/// PdfCraft patch: exported for its regression test (see [`SKIP_OFFSCREEN_PATHS`]).
564#[doc(hidden)]
565pub fn set_skip_offscreen_paths(skip: bool) {

569/// PdfCraft patch (30): what the renders on this thread have drawn offscreen, for tests that check
570/// a page's cost by counting rather than by timing it (see [`offscreen_draws`]).
571#[doc(hidden)]
572#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
573pub struct OffscreenDraws {
574    /// Tiling pattern cells drawn; a cell taken from `tiling_cells` isn't drawn again.
575    pub tiling_cells: u64,
576    /// The pixels of every pixmap drawn offscreen: tiling cells, masks, groups and the like.
577    pub pixels: u64,
578}
579
580thread_local! {
581    /// PdfCraft patch (30): see [`OffscreenDraws`].
582    static OFFSCREEN_DRAWS: std::cell::Cell<OffscreenDraws> =
583        const { std::cell::Cell::new(OffscreenDraws { tiling_cells: 0, pixels: 0 }) };
584}

586/// PdfCraft patch (30): exported for its regression tests (see [`OffscreenDraws`]). The counts
587/// only grow; a test takes the difference across a render.
588#[doc(hidden)]
589pub fn offscreen_draws() -> OffscreenDraws {
590    OFFSCREEN_DRAWS.try_with(std::cell::Cell::get).unwrap_or_default()
591}

593/// PdfCraft patch (30): a `width` × `height` pixmap to draw offscreen, counted in
594/// [`OffscreenDraws`]. Every pixmap the renderer renders into, besides the page, is made here.
595fn offscreen_pixmap(width: u16, height: u16, tiling_cell: bool) -> Pixmap {
596    // Gone only while the thread exits, when there is nothing left to count for.
597    let _ = OFFSCREEN_DRAWS.try_with(|draws| {
598        let mut counts = draws.get();
599        counts.pixels = counts.pixels.saturating_add(u64::from(width) * u64::from(height));
600        counts.tiling_cells = counts.tiling_cells.saturating_add(u64::from(tiling_cell));
601        draws.set(counts);
602    });
603    Pixmap::new(width, height)
604}

606/// PdfCraft patch: whether a device-space box can paint a pixel of a `width` × `height`
607/// canvas. A box whose bounds miss the canvas is skipped without changing a pixel.
608/// Bounds that aren't finite are drawn as before.
609fn paints_canvas(device: Rect, width: u16, height: u16) -> bool {
610    if !SKIP_OFFSCREEN_PATHS.with(std::cell::Cell::get) {
611        return true;
612    }
613    let finite = [device.x0, device.y0, device.x1, device.y1].iter().all(|v| v.is_finite());
614    !finite || (device.x0 < f64::from(width) && device.x1 > 0.0 && device.y0 < f64::from(height) && device.y1 > 0.0)
615}
616
617/// PdfCraft patch: whether a path drawn with `transform` can paint a pixel of a `width` ×
618/// `height` canvas. `reach` is how far its paint extends beyond the path, in user space: 0 for a
619/// fill; for a stroke, half its width times the larger of its miter limit (kurbo draws a miter
620/// only when its tip is within `limit × width / 2` of the vertex) and √2 (square caps). The box
621/// of the path's points and control points (a curve stays inside their hull) grown by that and
622/// [`DRAW_SLACK`], mapped to the device and grown by 2 pixels for antialiasing, contains
623/// everything it paints: a path whose box misses the canvas is skipped without changing a pixel,
624/// so a tile of a large page no longer strokes and fills every path on the page. Bounds that
625/// aren't finite (an empty path) are drawn as before.
626fn may_paint_canvas(path: &BezPath, transform: Affine, reach: f64, width: u16, height: u16) -> bool {
627    let mut points = Rect::new(f64::INFINITY, f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY);
628    let mut add = |p: Point| points = points.union_pt(p);
629    for el in path.elements() {
630        match *el {
631            kurbo::PathEl::MoveTo(p) | kurbo::PathEl::LineTo(p) => add(p),
632            kurbo::PathEl::QuadTo(c, p) => {
633                add(c);
634                add(p);
635            }
636            kurbo::PathEl::CurveTo(c1, c2, p) => {
637                add(c1);
638                add(c2);
639                add(p);
640            }
641            kurbo::PathEl::ClosePath => {}
642        }
643    }
644    let grow = reach + DRAW_SLACK;
645    let device = transform.transform_rect_bbox(points.inflate(grow, grow)).inflate(2.0, 2.0);
646    paints_canvas(device, width, height)
647}
648
649/// PdfCraft patch: whether a `rect` drawn with `transform` can paint a pixel of a `width` ×
650/// `height` canvas. Used for images: decoded data can only shrink against the stream-size box
651/// (subsampled `scale_factors`), so the box over-approximates what is drawn and skipping it
652/// never changes a pixel, while a tile of an image-heavy page no longer decodes, resamples and
653/// rasterizes every image on the page.
654fn may_paint_rect(rect: Rect, transform: Affine, width: u16, height: u16) -> bool {
655    let device = transform.transform_rect_bbox(rect.inflate(DRAW_SLACK, DRAW_SLACK)).inflate(2.0, 2.0);
656    paints_canvas(device, width, height)
657}
658
659/// PdfCraft patch: how far, in device pixels, the terms [`snap_minified_image`] drops may move an
660/// image's far edges: a hundredth of a pixel, which no edge shows. Rounding noise in a turned or
661/// scaled matrix stays far below it.
662const SNAP_SKEW: f64 = 0.01;
663
664/// PdfCraft patch: the whole-pixel device rectangle of a shrunk image whose axes lie along the
665/// device's, as `(width, height, transform)`: the size to shrink it to (along its own axes) and
666/// the transform that draws that raster 1:1, one source-axis step a whole device pixel. Upright,
667/// mirrored and quarter-turned images all qualify, so a page under `/Rotate` (or an image placed
668/// turned) is drawn as sharply as upright (#5530). `transform` maps source pixels to device
669/// pixels and `planned` is the size [`image_resampling_size`] chose; `None` (draw as before) for
670/// skewed or freely rotated images, non-finite geometry, or a snapped size that strays more than
671/// a pixel from `planned` (so the memory budget that size passed still holds). An image counts
672/// as axis-aligned when the terms the snap drops move its far edges by at most [`SNAP_SKEW`]: a
673/// tolerance on the coefficients alone let a slight skew of a very wide image through, though it
674/// moved the far edge by more than a pixel.
675fn snap_minified_image(transform: &Affine, source: (u32, u32), planned: (u32, u32)) -> Option<(u32, u32, Affine)> {
676    let [a, b, c, d, e, f] = transform.as_coeffs();
677    // Halves round up, not away from zero: a tile's origin moves edges by whole pixels, and only
678    // then do they snap where the whole page snaps them (-2.5 must go to -2 as 2.5 goes to 3).
679    let snap = |v: f64| (v + 0.5).floor();
680    // The device span of a source edge from `origin` across `side` samples of `scale`, rounded.
681    let edge = |origin: f64, scale: f64, side: u32| {
682        let (p, q) = (snap(origin), snap(origin + scale * f64::from(side)));
683        let (lo, hi) = (p.min(q), p.max(q));
684        (hi - lo >= 1.0 && lo.abs() < 1e6 && hi.abs() < 1e6).then_some((lo, hi))
685    };
686    // Along an axis drawn backwards (negative scale), the raster starts at the span's far end.
687    let start = |scale: f64, (lo, hi): (f64, f64)| if scale > 0.0 { lo } else { hi };
688    let step = |scale: f64| if scale > 0.0 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
689    // How far a dropped term moves the image's far edge: `scale` across `side` source samples.
690    let negligible = |scale: f64, side: u32| (scale * f64::from(side)).abs() <= SNAP_SKEW;
691    let (width, height) = source;
692    // Source x along device x, source y along device y (upright or mirrored), or a quarter turn:
693    // source x along device y, source y along device x.
694    let (w, h, draw) = if negligible(b, width) && negligible(c, height) {
695        let (x, y) = (edge(e, a, source.0)?, edge(f, d, source.1)?);
696        // Bounded by the 1e6 check above, so the casts cannot saturate.
697        let (w, h) = ((x.1 - x.0) as u32, (y.1 - y.0) as u32);
698        (w, h, Affine::new([step(a), 0.0, 0.0, step(d), start(a, x), start(d, y)]))
699    } else if negligible(a, width) && negligible(d, height) {
700        let (x, y) = (edge(e, c, source.1)?, edge(f, b, source.0)?);
701        let (w, h) = ((y.1 - y.0) as u32, (x.1 - x.0) as u32);
702        (w, h, Affine::new([0.0, step(b), step(c), 0.0, start(c, x), start(b, y)]))
703    } else {
704        return None;
705    };
706    (w.abs_diff(planned.0) <= 1 && h.abs_diff(planned.1) <= 1).then_some((w, h, draw))
707}

718/// PdfCraft patch (27): the most device pixels of a group blended in CMYK at once (2^24, a 4096 ×
719/// 4096 square). Each costs about 16 bytes while its band is blended (two pass canvases, its
720/// tints and their RGB); a larger group is blended in bands of whole rows under it, and only

778/// PdfCraft patch (30): the cell pixmaps of coloured tiling patterns, keyed by the setting of the
779/// pattern (`TilingPattern::instance`) and the cell's size and scale. A page that fills many
780/// shapes with one pattern (pdf.js issue 8078 paints 73,047 stencil masks with a pattern whose
781/// cell is 3.5 MB) drew and kept a cell per fill, which ran out of memory; the fills now share
782/// one. A handful of entries covers a run of fills with one pattern, and bounds what the cache
783/// keeps besides what the scene holds anyway.
784#[derive(Default)]
785struct TilingCells(Vec<(TilingCellKey, Arc<Pixmap>)>);
786
787#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
788struct TilingCellKey {
789    instance: u64,
790    /// Whether this is the bordered cell of a pattern whose step shows one cell (patch (20)).
791    one_cell: bool,
792    is_stroke: bool,
793    pixels: (u16, u16),
794    scale: (u64, u64),
795}
796
797impl TilingCells {
798    const MAX_ENTRIES: usize = 8;
799
800    fn get(&self, key: &TilingCellKey) -> Option<Arc<Pixmap>> {
801        self.0.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == key).map(|(_, cell)| cell.clone())
802    }
803
804    fn insert(&mut self, key: TilingCellKey, cell: Arc<Pixmap>) {
805        if self.0.len() >= Self::MAX_ENTRIES {
806            self.0.remove(0);
807        }
808        self.0.push((key, cell));
809    }
810}

812/// PdfCraft patch (27): which inks a pass of a `DeviceCMYK` group draws, and whether the
813/// group asked for something a pass can't draw.
814///
815/// A pass paints the complement of ink tints as colour — no ink is white — so the RGB blend
816/// functions compute ISO 32000-2 §11.3.4's subtractive blend, `1 − B(1 − cb, 1 − cs)`, and
817/// complementing the pixels back gives the tints. The cyan, magenta and yellow pass paints
818/// them as red, green and blue, which is also how §11.3.5.3 has the nonseparable modes treat
819/// them. The black pass paints black ink as a grey, so a separable mode blends it like any
820/// tint, and of the nonseparable modes Hue, Saturation and Color keep the backdrop's grey
821/// while Luminosity takes the source's: §11.3.5.3's rule for the K component.
822#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
823struct InkState {
824    pass: Option<InkPass>,
825    /// Something in the group has no ink tints (a pattern, an image, an ICCBased CMYK colour):
826    /// the group is drawn as before instead.
827    unsupported: bool,
828}
829
830#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
831enum InkPass {
832    /// Cyan, magenta and yellow as red, green and blue.
833    Cmy,
834    /// Black as grey.
835    K,
836}
837
838impl InkState {
839    /// The colour a pass paints for `color`; transparent, with the group marked unsupported,
840    /// when the colour has no ink tints.
841    fn paint(&mut self, pass: InkPass, color: &Color) -> AlphaColor<Srgb> {
842        let Some(([c, m, y, k], alpha)) = color.ink_tints() else {
843            self.unsupported = true;
844            return AlphaColor::TRANSPARENT;
845        };
846        match pass {
847            InkPass::Cmy => AlphaColor::new([1.0 - c, 1.0 - m, 1.0 - y, alpha]),
848            InkPass::K => AlphaColor::new([1.0 - k, 1.0 - k, 1.0 - k, alpha]),
849        }
850    }
851}
852
853#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
854enum ImagePixelFormat {
855    Luma,
856    Rgb,
857    Rgba,
858}
859
860impl Renderer {
861    /// PdfCraft patch (22): whether the innermost transparency group is a knockout group.
862    fn in_knockout(&self) -> bool {
863        self.knockout.last().copied().unwrap_or(false)
864    }
865
866    /// PdfCraft patch (26): the blend-mode pass of the innermost group, when that group is a
867    /// knockout group drawn in passes, so the element now drawn is one of its own elements.
868    fn knockout_pass(&mut self) -> Option<&mut KnockoutPass> {
869        let depth = self.knockout.len();
870        if !self.in_knockout() {
871            return None;
872        }
873        self.knockout_passes.last_mut().filter(|pass| pass.depth == depth)
874    }
875
876    /// PdfCraft patch (26): whether an element of blend mode `mode` belongs to another pass than
877    /// the current one, so here it clears what is under its shape instead of painting. Records
878    /// the mode for its own pass.
879    fn knockout_pass_skips(&mut self, mode: BlendMode) -> bool {
880        let Some(pass) = self.knockout_pass() else {
881            return false;
882        };
883        if mode == pass.mode {
884            return false;
885        }
886        if !pass.other_modes.contains(&mode) {
887            pass.other_modes.push(mode);
888        }
889        true
890    }
891
892    pub(crate) fn new(
893        width: u16,
894        height: u16,
895        settings: RenderSettings,
896        cache: &RenderCache<'_>,
897        color_replacement: Option<ColorReplacement>,
898        preview: bool,
899    ) -> Self {
900        Self {
901            ctx: RenderContext::new_with(width, height, settings),
902            color_replacement,
903            in_annotations: false,
904            knockout: Vec::new(),
905            erasing: false,
906            knockout_passes: Vec::new(),
907            erase_groups: 0,
908            inside_pattern: false,
909            soft_mask_cache: HashMap::default(),
910            tiling_cells: TilingCells::default(),
911            outline_cache: cache.outline_cache.clone(),
912            cur_mask: None,
913            in_type3_glyph: false,
914            scaler: Scaler::new(ResamplingFunction::CatmullRom),
915            preview,
916            image_transparency_stack: Vec::new(),
917            ink: InkState::default(),
918        }
919    }
920
921    /// PdfCraft patch: returns the stroke's reach for [`may_paint_canvas`].
922    fn set_stroke_properties(&mut self, stroke_props: &StrokeProps, is_text: bool, path: &BezPath) -> f64 {
923        let threshold = if is_text { 0.25 } else { 1.0 };
924
925        // Best-effort attempt to ensure a line width of at least 1.0, as required by the PDF
926        // specification. If we are stroking text, we reduce the threshold as it will otherwise
927        // lead to very bold-looking text at low resolutions.
928        let min_factor = max_factor(self.ctx.transform());
929        let mut line_width = stroke_props.line_width.max(0.01);
930        let transformed_width = line_width * min_factor;
931
932        // Only enforce line width if not inside of pattern or type 3 glyph.
933        if transformed_width < threshold && !self.inside_pattern && !self.in_type3_glyph {
934            line_width /= transformed_width;
935            line_width *= threshold;
936        }
937
938        // PdfCraft patch: a stroke far wider than the canvas looks the same as one a few canvases
939        // wide, but its geometry grows with the width: a fuzzed `/LW 9223372036854775807`
940        // allocated 10 GB in stroke expansion.
941        let widest = 4.0 * (f32::from(self.ctx.width()) + f32::from(self.ctx.height()));
942        if min_factor.is_finite() && min_factor > 0.0 && line_width * min_factor > widest {
943            line_width = widest / min_factor;
944        }
945
946        let stroke = kurbo::Stroke {
947            width: line_width as f64,
948            join: stroke_props.line_join,
949            miter_limit: stroke_props.miter_limit as f64,
950            start_cap: stroke_props.line_cap,
951            end_cap: stroke_props.line_cap,
952            // PdfCraft patch: see `usable_dash_pattern`.
953            dash_pattern: usable_dash_pattern(path, &stroke_props.dash_array).into(),
954            dash_offset: if stroke_props.dash_offset.is_finite() { stroke_props.dash_offset as f64 } else { 0.0 },
955        };
956
957        let reach = stroke_reach(&stroke);
958        self.ctx.set_stroke(stroke);
959        reach
960    }
961
962    fn draw_image_with_alpha_mask(&mut self, image_data: ImageData, mut alpha_data: LumaData) {
963        // PdfCraft patch: mismatched masks need a dummy RGB staging image. Validate and
964        // reserve it before creating/pushing any mask, so failure skips the whole image.
965        let Some(len) = source_byte_len(alpha_data.width, alpha_data.height, 3, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS) else {
966            log::warn!("Image alpha-mask staging dimensions exceeded the buffer limit; image skipped");
967            return;
968        };
969        let Some(mut dummy_rgb) = image_buffer(len) else {
970            log::warn!("Image alpha-mask staging buffer could not be allocated; image skipped");
971            return;
972        };
973        dummy_rgb.resize(len, 0);
974        let mask = {
975            let transform = *self.ctx.transform()
976                * Affine::scale_non_uniform(
977                    image_data.width() as f64 / alpha_data.width as f64,
978                    image_data.height() as f64 / alpha_data.height as f64,
979                );
980            // PdfCraft patch (#1649): a mask that differs in size from its image carries the
981            // shape on its own (Word saves text as a tiny black image with a glyph-bitmap mask).
982            // Shrunk by nearest-neighbour it keeps one sample in N and drops every stroke thinner
983            // than N mask pixels, so a shrunk mask is filtered whatever its `/Interpolate`, which
984            // only asks for smoothing when the mask is enlarged.
985            let (x, y) = x_y_advances(&transform);
986            if x.length() < 1.0 || y.length() < 1.0 {
987                alpha_data.interpolate = true;
988            }
989            let mut renderer = Self {
990                ctx: RenderContext::new_with(self.ctx.width(), self.ctx.height(), derive_settings(self.ctx.render_settings())),
991                // PdfCraft patch: this renders an image's alpha mask, which must keep its
992                // original values, so it is never remapped by the reading-colours setting.
993                color_replacement: None,
994                in_annotations: false,
995                knockout: Vec::new(),
996                erasing: false,
997                knockout_passes: Vec::new(),
998                erase_groups: 0,
999                inside_pattern: false,
1000                soft_mask_cache: HashMap::default(),
1001                tiling_cells: TilingCells::default(),
1002                outline_cache: self.outline_cache.clone(),
1003                cur_mask: None,
1004                in_type3_glyph: false,
1005                scaler: self.scaler,
1006                preview: self.preview,
1007                image_transparency_stack: Vec::new(),
1008                ink: InkState::default(),
1009            };
1010            let mut mask_pix = offscreen_pixmap(self.ctx.width(), self.ctx.height(), false);
1011            let rgb_data = ImageData::Rgb(RgbData {
1012                data: dummy_rgb,
1013                width: alpha_data.width,
1014                height: alpha_data.height,
1015                interpolate: alpha_data.interpolate,
1016                scale_factors: alpha_data.scale_factors,
1017            });
1018            renderer.ctx.set_transform(transform);
1019            // Note that there is a circle between `draw_image` and `draw_image_with_alpha_mask`,
1020            // but `draw_image_with_alpha_mask` is only called if the dimensions or interpolate
1021            // values between alpha_data and rgb_data don't match, which they do here.
1022            renderer.draw_image(rgb_data, Some(alpha_data));
1023            renderer.ctx.flush();
1024            let mut resources = crate::third_party::vello_cpu::Resources::default();
1025            renderer.ctx.render_to_pixmap(&mut resources, &mut mask_pix);
1026            Mask::new_alpha(&mask_pix)
1027        };
1028
1029        self.ctx.push_mask_layer(mask);
1030        self.image_transparency_stack.push(true);
1031        self.draw_image(image_data, None);
1032        self.image_transparency_stack.pop();
1033        self.ctx.pop_layer();
1034    }
1035
1036    fn resize_image_data(
1037        &self,
1038        data: Vec<u8>,
1039        src_width: u32,
1040        src_height: u32,
1041        new_width: u32,
1042        new_height: u32,
1043        pixel_format: ImagePixelFormat,
1044        interpolate: bool,
1045    ) -> (Vec<u8>, u32, u32) {
1046        // PdfCraft patch (#624): `/Interpolate` governs the pre-minification pass too. Using
1047        // Catmull-Rom here for an image that did not request interpolation blends hard edges
1048        // before ImageQuality::Low gets a chance to sample it. Keep the pre-resize (and its
1049        // bounded memory/performance behaviour), but use nearest-neighbour when interpolation
1050        // is disabled. PDF's default for `/Interpolate` is false.
1051        let nearest = Scaler::new(ResamplingFunction::Nearest);
1052        let scaler = if interpolate { &self.scaler } else { &nearest };
1053        let resized = match pixel_format {
1054            ImagePixelFormat::Luma => self.resize_image_data_impl::<1>(
1055                scaler,
1056                interpolate,
1057                data,
1058                src_width,
1059                src_height,
1060                new_width,
1061                new_height,
1062                |scaler, source_size, target_size| scaler.plan_planar_resampling(source_size, target_size),
1063            ),
1064            ImagePixelFormat::Rgb => self.resize_image_data_impl::<3>(
1065                scaler,
1066                interpolate,
1067                data,
1068                src_width,
1069                src_height,
1070                new_width,
1071                new_height,
1072                |scaler, source_size, target_size| scaler.plan_rgb_resampling(source_size, target_size),
1073            ),
1074            ImagePixelFormat::Rgba => self.resize_image_data_impl::<4>(
1075                scaler,
1076                interpolate,
1077                data,
1078                src_width,
1079                src_height,
1080                new_width,
1081                new_height,
1082                |scaler, source_size, target_size| scaler.plan_rgba_resampling(source_size, target_size, true),
1083            ),
1084        };
1085        match resized {
1086            Ok(out) => (out, new_width, new_height),
1087            Err(original) => {
1088                log::warn!("Image resampling failed or exceeded its buffer limit; falling back to source data");
1089                (original, src_width, src_height)
1090            }
1091        }
1092    }
1093
1094    fn resize_image_data_impl<const N: usize>(
1095        &self,
1096        scaler: &Scaler,
1097        interpolate: bool,
1098        data: Vec<u8>,
1099        src_width: u32,
1100        src_height: u32,
1101        new_width: u32,
1102        new_height: u32,
1103        plan: impl FnOnce(&Scaler, ImageSize, ImageSize) -> Result<Arc<Resampling<u8, N>>, PicScaleError>,
1104    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>> {
1105        // PdfCraft patch: validate before constructing a plan or allocating its output/scratch.
1106        // Returning the owned input preserves both its pixels and dimensions on any failure.
1107        let resized = (|| {
1108            let len = resampling_byte_len((src_width, src_height), (new_width, new_height), N, data.len(), MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS, interpolate)?;
1109            let source_size = ImageSize::new(src_width as usize, src_height as usize);
1110            let target_size = ImageSize::new(new_width as usize, new_height as usize);
1111            let src = ImageStore::<u8, N>::from_slice(&data, source_size.width, source_size.height).ok()?;
1112            let plan = plan(scaler, source_size, target_size).ok()?;
1113            let scratch_len = plan.scratch_size();
1114            // Nearest-neighbour needs no scratch, so any scratch it reports is refused.
1115            let scratch_bound =
1116                if interpolate { resampling_scratch_byte_len((src_width, src_height), (new_width, new_height), N, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS)? } else { 0 };
1117            if scratch_len > scratch_bound {
1118                return None;
1119            }
1120            let mut out = image_buffer(len)?;
1121            out.resize(len, 0);
1122            let mut dst = ImageStoreMut::<u8, N>::from_slice(&mut out, target_size.width, target_size.height).ok()?;
1123            let mut scratch = image_buffer(scratch_len)?;
1124            scratch.resize(scratch_len, 0);
1125            plan.resample_with_scratch(&src, &mut dst, &mut scratch).ok()?;
1126            Some(out)
1127        })();
1128        match resized {
1129            Some(out) => Ok(out),
1130            None => Err(data),
1131        }
1132    }
1133
1134    /// The size an image of `width` x `height` samples is decoded at to be drawn with
1135    /// `transform`, or `None` if `draw_image` skips it: off the canvas (PdfCraft patch: see
1136    /// `may_paint_rect`; checked before decoding, so a tile no longer decodes every image on its
1137    /// page), or, in a preview, covering only a few device pixels (PdfCraft patch; final renders
1138    /// always draw them). The tiny-image test measures axis lengths: the size returned maps a
1139    /// point, so it includes the translation and only suits the decode hint.
1140    fn image_draw_size(&self, width: u32, height: u32, transform: Affine) -> Option<(u32, u32)> {
1141        if !may_paint_rect(Rect::new(0.0, 0.0, f64::from(width), f64::from(height)), transform, self.ctx.width(), self.ctx.height()) {
1142            return None;
1143        }
1144        let target_width = (transform * Point::new(width as f64, 0.0)).to_vec2().length().ceil() as u32;
1145        let target_height = (transform * Point::new(0.0, height as f64)).to_vec2().length().ceil() as u32;
1146        if self.preview {
1147            let c = transform.as_coeffs();
1148            let tiny_w = (f64::from(width) * (c[0] * c[0] + c[1] * c[1]).sqrt()).ceil() as u32;
1149            let tiny_h = (f64::from(height) * (c[2] * c[2] + c[3] * c[3]).sqrt()).ceil() as u32;
1150            if tiny_w.saturating_mul(tiny_h) < PREVIEW_MIN_IMAGE_AREA {
1151                return None;
1152            }
1153        }
1154        Some((target_width, target_height))
1155    }
1156
1157    fn draw_image(&mut self, image_data: ImageData, alpha_data: Option<LumaData>) {
1158        let cur_transform = *self.ctx.transform();
1159        let (x_scale, y_scale) = {
1160            let (x, y) = x_y_advances(&cur_transform);
1161            (x.length() as f32, y.length() as f32)
1162        };
1163        // PdfCraft patch: do not send non-finite or collapsed geometry to the rasterizer.
1164        if !cur_transform.as_coeffs().iter().all(|v| v.is_finite())
1165            || !x_scale.is_finite()
1166            || !y_scale.is_finite()
1167            || x_scale <= 0.0
1168            || y_scale <= 0.0
1169        {
1170            log::warn!("Image has an invalid transform and was skipped");
1171            return;
1172        }
1173        let (source_width, source_height) = (image_data.width(), image_data.height());
1174        let channels = match &image_data {
1175            ImageData::Luma(_) => 1,
1176            ImageData::Rgb(_) => 3,
1177        };
1178        let data_len = match &image_data {
1179            ImageData::Luma(a) => a.data.len(),
1180            ImageData::Rgb(a) => a.data.len(),
1181        };
1182        if source_byte_len(source_width, source_height, channels, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS) != Some(data_len) {
1183            log::warn!("Image has invalid or over-limit source dimensions/data and was skipped");
1184            return;
1185        }
1186        let interpolate = image_data.interpolate();
1187        let requested_resize = x_scale < 1.0 || y_scale < 1.0;
1188        // PdfCraft patch: an image that did not ask for interpolation and is drawn below its
1189        // resolution is shrunk by area averaging (`area_shrink`), not nearest-neighbour, which
1190        // broke up the text of scans shown at screen size. Type 3 glyph images keep the nearest
1191        // shrink of #624: they are drawn with a frame of their own and never snapped.
1192        let area = !interpolate
1193            && requested_resize
1194            && !self.in_type3_glyph
1195            // Wider sources keep #624's bounded nearest-neighbour shrink (`area_shrink` refuses
1196            // them): skipping them, as a refused shrink at source size would, loses the image.
1197            && source_width.max(source_height) <= MAX_RESAMPLING_SOURCE_SIDE;
1198        let mut alpha_data = alpha_data;
1199        if let Some(a) = alpha_data.take() {
1200            if source_byte_len(a.width, a.height, 1, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS) != Some(a.data.len()) {
1201                log::warn!("Image has invalid or over-limit alpha dimensions/data and was skipped");
1202                return;
1203            }
1204            if a.width != source_width || a.height != source_height || a.interpolate != interpolate {
1205                // PdfCraft patch: a soft mask no larger than its area-shrunk image is sampled onto
1206                // the image's grid, so colour and mask are averaged together, premultiplied. Drawn
1207                // as a mask layer over the image instead, the averaged colour (transparent samples
1208                // included) was multiplied by the averaged mask, and the colour of transparent
1209                // samples showed at the mask's edges. A larger mask carries detail the image does
1210                // not (#1649) and keeps the layer.
1211                let on_grid = (area && a.width <= source_width && a.height <= source_height)
1212                    .then(|| mask_on_image_grid(&a, source_width, source_height))
1213                    .flatten();
1214                match on_grid {
1215                    Some(data) => {
1216                        alpha_data = Some(LumaData { data, width: source_width, height: source_height, interpolate, ..a });
1217                    }
1218                    None => {
1219                        self.draw_image_with_alpha_mask(image_data, a);
1220                        return;
1221                    }
1222                }
1223            } else {
1224                alpha_data = Some(a);
1225            }
1226        }
1227        let mut quality = if interpolate { ImageQuality::Medium } else { ImageQuality::Low };
1228        let has_alpha = alpha_data.is_some();
1229        let mut may_have_transparency = has_alpha || self.force_images_may_have_transparency();
1230        let (new_width, new_height) =
1231            match image_resampling_size(source_width, source_height, channels, data_len, x_scale, y_scale, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS, interpolate) {
1232                Some(target) => target,
1233                None => {
1234                    if image_byte_len(source_width, source_height, 4, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS).is_none() {
1235                        log::warn!("Image resampling exceeded its buffer limit and the original resolution cannot fit the backend; image skipped");
1236                        return;
1237                    }
1238                    log::warn!("Image resampling exceeded its buffer limit; retaining the original resolution");
1239                    (source_width, source_height)
1240                }
1241            };
1242        // PdfCraft patch (#624): High is bicubic and would blend the nearest pre-resize of an image
1243        // that did not request interpolation, so only interpolated glyph images are promoted.
1244        if requested_resize && self.in_type3_glyph && interpolate {
1245            quality = ImageQuality::High;
1246        }
1247        // PdfCraft patch: an image the size of a page scan is smoothed when drawn above its
1248        // resolution, even without `/Interpolate`: bilinearly, as images that ask for it are.
1249        // Scans rarely ask, and drawn nearest-neighbour each sample of a zoomed scan became a
1250        // block, so the edges of its text were staircases. Bicubic looked the same on a zoomed
1251        // 300 dpi scan and drew its tiles five times slower. Smaller images (icons, QR codes,
1252        // pixel art) keep their hard pixels. A scan shrunk on one side and stretched on the other
1253        // is smoothed too: the area shrink leaves the shrunk side at 1:1, where bilinear adds
1254        // nothing, and the stretched side would otherwise be drawn nearest-neighbour.
1255        if !interpolate
1256            && !self.in_type3_glyph
1257            && (x_scale > SMOOTHED_IMAGE_SCALE || y_scale > SMOOTHED_IMAGE_SCALE)
1258            && source_width.min(source_height) >= SMOOTHED_IMAGE_SIDE
1259        {
1260            quality = ImageQuality::Medium;
1261        }
1262        // PdfCraft patch: an image that is shrunk (filtered or area-averaged), with its axes along
1263        // the device's (upright, mirrored or a quarter turn), lands on whole device pixels. It is
1264        // shrunk once to exactly its snapped device rectangle and drawn 1:1 from the snapped
1265        // corner. Otherwise the shrunk raster (rounded up to a whole size) is sampled a second time
1266        // at a fractional scale and offset, which blurs scans and photos (or, by the nearest
1267        // sampler of a non-interpolated image, drops samples again).
1268        let snapped = if (interpolate || area) && requested_resize && !self.in_type3_glyph && (new_width, new_height) != (source_width, source_height)
1269        {
1270            snap_minified_image(&cur_transform, (source_width, source_height), (new_width, new_height))
1271        } else {
1272            None
1273        };
1274        let (new_width, new_height) = snapped.map_or((new_width, new_height), |s| (s.0, s.1));
1275        // PdfCraft patch: an area shrink never enlarges. A side drawn at or above its resolution
1276        // (an image shrunk across and stretched down, as a 204 × 98 dpi fax is, or a snapped side
1277        // rounded past its source) keeps its samples and is enlarged by the sampler; the snap
1278        // then no longer matches, so the full transform places the image.
1279        let (new_width, new_height) = if area { (new_width.min(source_width), new_height.min(source_height)) } else { (new_width, new_height) };
1280        let needs_resize = (new_width, new_height) != (source_width, source_height);
1281
1282        // PdfCraft patch (#624): a minified image with a soft mask that is neither interpolated nor
1283        // area-averaged (a Type 3 glyph image, or a source wider than MAX_RESAMPLING_SOURCE_SIDE)
1284        // is nearest-sampled straight into premultiplied target RGBA. That skips the
1285        // full-resolution RGBA copy below and the premultiply pass after it. PdfCraft patch: an
1286        // area-averaged one (a stencil's ink, or an image under its mask) skips them too, and is
1287        // premultiplied a source row at a time as it is averaged (`area_shrink_premultiplied`).
1288        let direct = match &alpha_data {
1289            Some(alpha) if needs_resize && !interpolate && !area => {
1290                nearest_premultiplied_rgba(&image_data, &alpha.data, (source_width, source_height), (new_width, new_height))
1291            }
1292            Some(alpha) if needs_resize && area => {
1293                area_shrink_premultiplied(&image_data, &alpha.data, (source_width, source_height), (new_width, new_height))
1294            }
1295            _ => None,
1296        };
1297        let mut premultiplied = direct.is_some();
1298        // Preserve the single-channel/RGB fast paths. With alpha, expand directly to RGBA;
1299        // every source and alpha length was validated before zipping or allocating.
1300        let (data, format) = match (direct, image_data, alpha_data) {
1301            (Some(rgba), _, _) => (rgba, ImagePixelFormat::Rgba),
1302            (None, ImageData::Luma(luma), None) => (luma.data, ImagePixelFormat::Luma),
1303            (None, ImageData::Rgb(rgb), None) => (rgb.data, ImagePixelFormat::Rgb),
1304            (None, image, Some(alpha)) => {
1305                let Some(len) = source_byte_len(source_width, source_height, 4, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS) else {
1306                    return;
1307                };
1308                let Some(mut rgba) = image_buffer(len) else {
1309                    log::warn!("Image RGBA buffer could not be allocated and the image was skipped");
1310                    return;
1311                };
1312                match image {
1313                    ImageData::Luma(luma) => {
1314                        rgba.extend(luma.data.iter().zip(alpha.data).flat_map(|(g, a)| [*g, *g, *g, a]));
1315                    }
1316                    ImageData::Rgb(rgb) => {
1317                        rgba.extend(rgb.data.as_chunks::<3>().0.iter().zip(alpha.data).flat_map(|([r, g, b], a)| [*r, *g, *b, a]));
1318                    }
1319                }
1320                (rgba, ImagePixelFormat::Rgba)
1321            }
1322        };
1323        let (data, mut img_width, mut img_height) = if premultiplied {
1324            (data, new_width, new_height)
1325        } else if needs_resize && area {
1326            let mut data = data;
1327            if matches!(format, ImagePixelFormat::Rgba) {
1328                // Averaging straight colours would bleed the colour of transparent samples into
1329                // their neighbours; premultiplied colours count each by its coverage.
1330                premultiply_rgba(&mut data);
1331                premultiplied = true;
1332            }
1333            area_resize(data, (source_width, source_height), (new_width, new_height), format)
1334        } else if needs_resize {
1335            self.resize_image_data(data, source_width, source_height, new_width, new_height, format, interpolate)
1336        } else {
1337            (data, source_width, source_height)
1338        };
1339        if image_byte_len(img_width, img_height, 4, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS).is_none() {
1340            log::warn!("Image resampling failed and the original resolution cannot fit the backend; image skipped");
1341            return;
1342        }
1343        let mut additional_transform = Affine::scale_non_uniform(source_width as f64 / img_width as f64, source_height as f64 / img_height as f64);
1344        let mut rgba_data = if matches!(format, ImagePixelFormat::Rgba) {
1345            data
1346        } else {
1347            let Some(len) = image_byte_len(img_width, img_height, 4, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS) else {
1348                return;
1349            };
1350            let Some(mut rgba) = image_buffer(len) else {
1351                log::warn!("Image RGBA buffer could not be allocated and the image was skipped");
1352                return;
1353            };
1354            match format {
1355                ImagePixelFormat::Luma => rgba.extend(data.iter().flat_map(|g| [*g, *g, *g, 255])),
1356                ImagePixelFormat::Rgb => rgba.extend(data.as_chunks::<3>().0.iter().flat_map(|[r, g, b]| [*r, *g, *b, 255])),
1357                ImagePixelFormat::Rgba => {} // Handled above.
1358            }
1359            rgba
1360        };
1361        if has_alpha && !premultiplied {
1362            premultiply_rgba(&mut rgba_data);
1363        }
1364        // Type 3 glyphs get a transparent two-pixel frame for interpolation. Check the padded
1365        // RGBA allocation and u16 dimensions too, before narrowing or growing either side.
1366        if self.in_type3_glyph {
1367            let (Some(width), Some(height)) = (img_width.checked_add(4), img_height.checked_add(4)) else {
1368                return;
1369            };
1370            let Some(len) = image_byte_len(width, height, 4, MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS) else {
1371                log::warn!("Image glyph padding exceeded its buffer limit and the image was skipped");
1372                return;
1373            };
1374            let Some(mut padded) = image_buffer(len) else {
1375                log::warn!("Image glyph padding could not be allocated and the image was skipped");
1376                return;
1377            };
1378            let row_len = width as usize * 4; // Checked RGBA length above bounds every row.
1379            padded.resize(row_len * 2, 0);
1380            for row in rgba_data.chunks_exact(img_width as usize * 4) {
1381                padded.extend([0; 8]);
1382                padded.extend_from_slice(row);
1383                padded.extend([0; 8]);
1384            }
1385            padded.resize(len, 0);
1386            (img_width, img_height) = (width, height);
1387            additional_transform *= Affine::translate((-2.0, -2.0));
1388            may_have_transparency = true;
1389            rgba_data = padded;
1390        }
1391        let pixmap = Pixmap::from_parts_with_opacity(bytemuck::cast_vec(rgba_data), img_width as u16, img_height as u16, may_have_transparency);
1392        // The snapped transform draws the raster 1:1, so it holds only if the shrink produced the
1393        // snapped size. A failed resize hands back the source raster: drawn 1:1 it would come out
1394        // at its source size, so it keeps the full transform instead.
1395        let draw_transform = match snapped {
1396            Some((w, h, draw)) if (img_width, img_height) == (w, h) => draw,
1397            _ => cur_transform * additional_transform,
1398        };
1399        self.draw_pixmap(Arc::new(pixmap), quality, draw_transform);
1400    }
1401
1402    /// PdfCraft patch (30): the cell pixmap of tiling pattern `t`, `size` pixels drawn at
1403    /// `initial_transform`; a cell with a `key` is drawn once and then taken from `tiling_cells`.
1404    fn tiling_cell(
1405        &mut self,
1406        t: &crate::third_party::hayro_interpret::pattern::TilingPattern<'_>,
1407        key: Option<TilingCellKey>,
1408        size: (u16, u16),
1409        initial_transform: Affine,
1410        is_stroke: bool,
1411    ) -> Arc<Pixmap> {
1412        if let Some(cell) = key.and_then(|key| self.tiling_cells.get(&key)) {
1413            return cell;
1414        }
1415        let mut renderer = Self {
1416            ctx: RenderContext::new_with(size.0, size.1, derive_settings(self.ctx.render_settings())),
1417            // PdfCraft patch: a pattern cell is painted as one artwork, so its content is never
1418            // remapped by the reading-colours setting.
1419            color_replacement: None,
1420            in_annotations: false,
1421            knockout: Vec::new(),
1422            erasing: false,
1423            knockout_passes: Vec::new(),
1424            erase_groups: 0,
1425            cur_mask: None,
1426            inside_pattern: true,
1427            soft_mask_cache: HashMap::default(),
1428            tiling_cells: TilingCells::default(),
1429            outline_cache: self.outline_cache.clone(),
1430            in_type3_glyph: false,
1431            scaler: self.scaler,
1432            preview: self.preview,
1433            image_transparency_stack: Vec::new(),
1434            ink: InkState::default(),
1435        };
1436        t.interpret(&mut renderer, initial_transform, is_stroke);
1437        let mut pix = offscreen_pixmap(size.0, size.1, true);
1438        renderer.ctx.flush();
1439        let mut resources = crate::third_party::vello_cpu::Resources::default();
1440        renderer.ctx.render_to_pixmap(&mut resources, &mut pix);
1441        let pix = Arc::new(pix);
1442        if let Some(key) = key {
1443            self.tiling_cells.insert(key, pix.clone());
1444        }
1445        pix
1446    }
1447
1448    fn push_clip_path_inner(&mut self, clip_path: &BezPath, fill: FillRule) {
1449        let old_transform = *self.ctx.transform();
1450
1451        self.ctx.set_fill_rule(convert_fill_rule(fill));
1452        self.ctx.set_transform(Affine::IDENTITY);
1453        self.ctx.push_clip_path(clip_path);
1454
1455        self.ctx.set_transform(old_transform);
1456    }
1457
1458    fn draw_pixmap(&mut self, pixmap: Arc<Pixmap>, quality: ImageQuality, transform: Affine) {
1459        let (width, height) = (pixmap.width(), pixmap.height());
1460        let image = Image {
1461            image: ImageSource::Pixmap(pixmap),
1462            sampler: ImageSampler { x_extend: peniko::Extend::Pad, y_extend: peniko::Extend::Pad, quality, alpha: 1.0 },
1463        };
1464
1465        self.ctx.set_transform(transform);
1466        self.ctx.set_paint(image);
1467        self.ctx.fill_rect(&Rect::new(0.0, 0.0, width as f64, height as f64));
1468    }
